item.title: Xi unveils five initiatives for stronger BRICS
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
Xi unveils five initiatives for stronger BRICS Deeper cooperation essential for greater progress, president says President Xi Jinping unveiled five initiatives — covering the areas of artificial intelligence, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry, smart manufacturing, and talent development — to deepen practical cooperation among BRICS countries and bolster the collective strength of the Global South. Addressing the second session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi as he wrapped up his two-day participation in the gathering on Sunday, Xi stressed that a stronger foundation for cooperation was essential for the expanded grouping to achieve greater progress. He urged BRICS countries to leverage their close ties with emerging markets and Global South countries, pursuing open cooperation for mutual benefit while safeguarding stable and smooth industrial and supply chains. They should foster a larger integrated market, build incubators for innovation, upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging industries and deploy future industries, Xi added. China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, and it will support cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open AI ecosystem, Xi said. He proposed a BRICS special economic zone partnership under which countries could set up an intelligent portal, coordinate policies and build a new frontier for open development. China will also host the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation. Furthermore, China will push for the establishment of a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform and conduct digital skills training, technological exchanges and industrial alignment to jointly advance the digital economy, Xi said. He expressed the country's readiness to assist fellow BRICS countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, jointly promoting manufacturing transformation and upgrading. Xi also proposed a BRICS engineer cultivation alliance for the joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards. China will launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation to cultivate more high-caliber talent. Noting that this year marks the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), Xi said China will continue to pursue high-quality development, expand high-standard opening-up, implement the Global Development Initiative and advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation to share opportunities and prosper together with other countries. Liu Ying, a researcher at the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University of China, said that as BRICS marks its 20th anniversary and moves toward its next "golden decade", China's five initiatives respond to the shared development needs of BRICS and the wider Global South. China has offered not just directions for cooperation, but also concrete platforms and mechanisms to implement it, she said, helping BRICS countries expand their international voice while strengthening their own development foundations. Openness and inclusiveness in AI especially matter, Liu said, as open-source cooperation, large-model development and talent training can help Global South countries access and apply AI as a foundational resource for national development — an effort that China's strengths in technology, industry and application can help make possible. China is practicing "developmental multilateralism" — combining capacity building with real development outcomes to help the Global South participate more fully in the new wave of technological and industrial change, and ultimately pushing the global system toward a fairer, more inclusive and balanced order, Liu added. As the Global South, with its collective rise, has become a key driver of world multipolarity, Xi said that to bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, be an active, stabilizing and positive force in international affairs, and advance the well-being of all humanity. He stressed that Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguarding sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs and the peaceful settlement of disputes, to ensure that international law and international rules are applied to all, free from double standards. Xi emphasized the need to uphold multilateralism and the authority and role of the United Nations, and to support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency. World Trade Organization reform should proceed in the right direction, while the international financial architecture must be reformed and improved to increase developing countries' representation and voice, he added. Global South countries should remain committed to a people-centered development philosophy and strive to deliver on the UN's 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, he said. Addressing shared challenges, Xi said that Global South countries should work together to strengthen security governance, tackle traditional and nontraditional threats, and improve global climate governance. BRICS draws its growing influence from an inclusive approach that respects different development paths and promotes shared economic gains, said Lan Qingxin, director of the BRICS Research Center at the University of International Business and Economics in Beijing. Contact the writers at zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Beijing right in your palm
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
A robot rock band jammed as onlookers snapped photos, and an AI photo booth dressed visitors in traditional Chinese costumes, while AR glasses translated conversations in real time. And a new platform promises to put all of Beijing — visas, subways, shops, temples, and hidden hutong alleyways — in the palm of your hand. This was the scene at Beijing's Shougang Park last week, as the World Conference on Tourism Cooperation and Development 2026 drew representatives from over 50 countries and regions, dozens of cities, international organizations, and cross-border travel companies for a three-day event themed "Smart Tourism, Shared Prosperity". The event's sixth edition, hosted by the World Tourism Cities Federation and co-organized by the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism, concluded on Friday. The event was part of the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services. Expanding outreach A highlight was the launch of China Bound·Beijing, an English-language cultural tourism platform rolled out by China Daily in cooperation with the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism. It includes a website (chinabound.cn/beijing) and dedicated pages on China Bound's Alipay and WeChat mini-programs, offering everything from itinerary planning to inspiring destination profiles and AI-powered field assistance. Zheng Fang, deputy director of the Beijing culture and tourism bureau, describes it as a one-stop gateway for overseas visitors. "Through this platform, we hope to provide our overseas audiences with authoritative, firsthand information and updates about Beijing tourism," Zheng says. "The platform also provides a wide range of information about visas, transportation, shopping, scenic attractions, events, and other aspects of Beijing travel. We hope this will help international visitors plan their trips before coming to Beijing and provide them with comprehensive support throughout the process," she explains. "It's an important step in Beijing's efforts to expand its communications and outreach to international markets actively. We hope our friends overseas will find this platform useful, and that we earn the love and support of visitors from around the world." Joseph Daniel Lema, a professor at the College of Hospitality, the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, hails the platform's potential. "This makes travel easier and more accessible. It saves people time and inconvenience. I think it's going to be a real boon for the future," he says. "It's going to help tell the narrative of Beijing. This is a very ancient, historic city, so there's lots to talk about here; there's lots to learn. This app is going to help do that." Lema notes that the China Bound. Beijing release builds on a broader application introduced earlier this year. What excites him most, he says, is how the platform connects the dots of a traveler's journey — from the moment of inspiration to the final transaction. "Connecting a lot of the services has been a challenge for tourism for a long time. How do we connect everything from transportation to entry to exit, from food and beverage to events and entertainment? This app will be very valuable for a seamless experience," Lema says. He believes its timing is significant. "This is what the new generations coming up want. They're on their phones, and they want a seamless experience … people want to learn, and this is another channel to bring that all together." It'll help Beijing show its true self to the world, Lema says. "It's going to be a good asset for Beijing, and it also introduces the latest technologies," he says. "Many people don't realize how advanced the technology is here. China Bound is bringing everything together, from initial curiosity and travel searches to deciding where to go, and managing the experience while you're here, then following up and satisfaction, and so on. These apps can have the capabilities to do all of that."

item.title: China scales up embodied AI's reach
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
China scales up embodied AI's reach Vast industrial base, dense supply chains boosting robot performance Microduck, a robot duck that waddles, carries objects with its beak and skates on tiny wheels, has become an unlikely global AI hit. Priced at disarmingly $399, the gadget drew orders of as many as 10,000 units within days of its launch, with sales topping $2.6 million in the first 24 hours. Interestingly, it was developed by French robotics developer Pollen Robotics, part of New York-based AI platform Hugging Face, but it runs on a chip from China's Rockchip, and is manufactured in China by Shenzhen, Guangdong province-based firm Seeed Studio, according to media reports. Behind the toy-like duck is a much bigger technological shift. The global AI race is moving from models that generate words and images into embodied AI — robots that can perceive, reason and act in the physical world — and China is betting that its vast manufacturing base, dense supply chains and rapidly expanding robot fleet can give it an edge. This transition was on vivid display across Beijing in August. At the 2026 World Robot Conference, 373 companies packed exhibition halls with more than 3,000 products, including 311 debuts. Days later, more than 2,000 robots descended on the World Humanoid Robot Games, where they sprinted, fought, danced and tackled tasks drawn from factories, homes and service industries. Taken together, the events captured a Chinese robotics industry trying to make a crucial transition: from machines that look impressive on stage to machines that can earn their keep on factory floors. For much of the generative-AI boom, the competitive scoreboard was relatively straightforward: advanced semiconductors, computing clusters, foundation models, data and developers. Robots complicate that equation. A humanoid may need a sophisticated AI model, but it also needs motors, reducers, bearings, cameras, tactile sensors, batteries, power electronics, precision-machined joints and hands capable of manipulating objects. All of those components must work together reliably, repeatedly and cheaply. China already operates the world's largest industrial robot market and has spent decades building electronics, electric-vehicle and automation supply chains that can increasingly be redirected toward embodied AI. Components refined for smartphones and cars — cameras, batteries, sensors, motors and power electronics — are now turning up inside robots. Xi Ning, chair professor of robotics and automation at the University of Hong Kong, said at the World Robot Conference that China's gap with the United States in basic robotics theories and methods had shifted from one of "quality" toward one more of "quantity", while parts of China's supply chain had already moved ahead.

item.title: Training cooperation builds skills across bloc
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
Training cooperation builds skills across bloc Four years after the BRICS Technical and Vocational Education and Training Cooperation Alliance was set up, it has grown into a platform that mirrors the technical and vocational education and training priorities of each member country. As such, it offers a space for policy dialogue, knowledge exchange and joint capacity-building. The alliance, which has 97 institutions as its members and is managed by the China Education Association for International Exchange in Beijing, translates high-level BRICS consensus into grassroots people-to-people collaboration, said Yang Jun, vice-president and secretary-general of the association. Its work has been acknowledged in summit documents from the 14th to the 17th BRICS summits. Most recently, the declaration of the 13th BRICS Ministers of Education Meeting in Bhubaneswar, India, adopted on Aug 7, highlighted its work in joint projects, information sharing and collective upgrading of technical and vocational education and training. The alliance adopts a multistakeholder governance model involving governments, industry associations, training institutions and companies, Yang said. This has enabled a series of practical initiatives — policy dialogues, best-practice sharing, faculty exchanges, student engagement and industry-academia matchmaking — and it has steadily expanded its activities, membership and influence, he said. Since 2022, annual hybrid forums have been hosted by each rotating BRICS chair, with sessions held in Beijing, Johannesburg, Moscow, Brasilia and New Delhi. Discussions have focused on skills related to the green economy, sustainable workforce development and inclusive digital transformation for technical and vocational education and training, creating a recurring high-level dialogue channel for practitioners across the member states, Yang said. Youth mobility and skills development form another core pillar. Three sessions of the Rising Star TVET Student Camp have brought together more than 100 young participants from BRICS countries. The program includes keynote speeches, cross-cultural youth panels, corporate site visits and cultural immersion, helping young professionals expand international peer networks and sharpen job-ready competencies, he said. One participant, Fatimah Rashed N. Almahasheer from Saudi Arabia, said the camp "unites youth from diverse backgrounds to share perspectives and brainstorm innovative solutions to shared global challenges". Another participant, Yeaymrokal Kebede Mola from Ethiopia, said the alliance creates opportunities for young people to engage in meaningful dialogue, discuss ideas and collaborate on projects related to important global issues. Goitsemang Itlotleng Maledu of South Africa said BRICS members stand to gain collectively through better infrastructure, trade finance and strengthened science, engineering and technical capacities. To improve teaching quality across the network, the alliance has run 12 online workshops and seminars for faculty members and institutional administrators, Yang said. With the help of 50 international specialists, these sessions have covered digital-resource building, industry-education integration, curriculum design and teaching evaluation, reaching more than 1,000 teaching and managerial staff, he said. Joint research has also become a cornerstone. Last year, the alliance published a report that examined technical and vocational education and training in various countries and the implications for economic development. Work on a second-phase research project began this year, with participation extended to the new BRICS-plus members Ethiopia, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, Yang said. zoushuo@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: As Mid-Autumn Festival nears, mooncakes return
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
Ding Shumin, a Beijing native in her 60s, stood at the counter of a pastry shop in Beijing, carefully selecting mooncakes. One for herself, another for a relative, a few for friends — and some for her grandson. By the time she left the shop, Ding had packed about 20. She could have chosen chocolate, durian and some other contemporary flavors. Instead, she stuck to the taste she has loved since childhood: wuren, a traditional filling made with nuts and seeds. "When I was little, eating mooncakes was one of the things I looked forward to most at Mid-Autumn Festival," Ding said. "Wuren was always my favorite. Even now, I still have to buy some." The packaging of the mooncakes invoked as much nostalgia as the taste. Five mooncakes were first bundled in brown kraft paper, then wrapped in bright red paper bearing the shop's name and the flavor in black calligraphy, before being tied with coarse twine. There was no elaborate gift box — just a humble wrapping that has survived from another era. With Mid-Autumn Festival around the corner on Sept 25, old-fashioned mooncakes are a familiar sight in Beijing, and bakeries are competing for attention with their increasingly inventive flavors. For Li Baozhi, who is in his 50s, has been in the trade for decades and now works with the pastry shop of Ya'er Liji, a time-honored halal food brand known for traditional Beijing flavors, the appeal of the traditional varieties lies in their simplicity. Li began learning to make mooncakes when he was about 20 years old. He remembers the earliest versions as plain, firm and crumbly. "The oldest style may have been made simply with sugar, oil and flour," Li said. "You put the mooncake into a square mold, pressed it flat, knocked it out of the mold and then baked it." Today, Li makes traditional fillings including wuren, black sesame, red bean and jujube paste, which he said are most popular among buyers. The pastry is also distinctly different from the soft, syrupy crust of Cantonese-style mooncakes. "Cantonese-style mooncakes feature a lot of filling and thin skin, while Beijing-style ones have thicker, crispy skin and less filling," Li said. Wuren, he added, is particularly popular among older customers. But preserving tradition does not mean freezing it in time. "Although it is traditional, it still has to be improved. Otherwise, it won't work," he said. For Li, mooncakes are part of the rhythm of everyday Chinese life — much like dumplings at Spring Festival and zongzi, or sticky rice dumplings, during Dragon Boat Festival. A mooncake that costs just a few yuan can carry more meaning than an expensive gift box, he noted. That down-to-earth quality may be precisely what gives traditional mooncakes staying power. In the past, mooncakes were a precious seasonal treat because food was less abundant. Today, they have to compete with a seemingly endless menu of alternatives — including flavors that earlier generations could hardly have imagined. "The sales were even stronger in the past, because there was less choice," Li said. "But now people have more options — you can eat mooncakes, or hairy crabs instead." Yet the ritual has proved difficult to replace. At the bakery where customer Ding shopped, several thousand mooncakes are sold daily, according to Ding Shilong, the restaurant's culinary director. At the busiest point before the festival, sales can climb to 10,000 or even 20,000 pieces a day. In nearby Qianmen, a historic district in central Beijing, 53-year-old Zhai Guangjun runs another traditional bakery tucked inside a hutong. He started selling mooncakes about a month before the festival, with most customers coming from the neighborhood. For many, Zhai said, buying old-fashioned mooncakes is less about novelty than memory — a small edible link to childhood and to the annual promise of family reunions. Mooncake fillings vary widely across China, from Beijing's traditional wuren and jujube pastes to Shanghai's savory fresh meat fillings and the rich lotus seed paste in Guangdong province. The same tension between tradition and novelty plays out elsewhere in China too. On Sept 8, Russian influencer Marina Maloy, who lives in Shanghai, posted a video of herself sampling mooncakes on Nanjing East Road. Alongside the city's classic fresh meat mooncakes, she tried newer versions flavored with fermented red bean curd sauce, shrimp and crab roe (the rich, golden substance found inside a crab). After sampling her way through the mooncakes, Maloy said the experience gave her a glimpse of people's "respect for tradition and their love of life".

item.title: Africa eyes initiative in disease control
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Africa eyes initiative in disease control Interoperability with existing systems can help enable more timely decisions Health cooperation among BRICS countries could help Africa close persistent gaps in disease surveillance, research, diagnostics and vaccine production while strengthening health systems and improving access to medical products across the Global South, according to experts. The potential benefits are drawing attention as plans advance for a BRICS Integrated Early Warning System for the Prevention and Response to Mass Infectious Diseases. The initiative is aimed at strengthening disease detection, information sharing, preparedness and coordinated responses to future outbreaks. At the 16th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting in Chandigarh, India, in July, member nations supported the establishment of a dedicated sub-working group on the early warning system to advance the initiative, which is considered a milestone in advancing regional and international health security. For Africa, the proposed system could make an important contribution, particularly if it connects effectively with surveillance and early warning systems already in operation across the continent. "In an outbreak, speed matters enormously. The earlier we identify an unusual signal, the greater our chance of containing it before it becomes a much larger emergency," said Saran Koly, director of communication and public information for the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. She said the fast sharing of epidemiological information, laboratory results, genomic data and risk assessments across countries could improve the ability to identify and contain emerging threats. Koly said the priority for Africa should be ensuring interoperability between the BRICS-proposed early warning system and existing continental and national health structures in Africa. "We already have national public-health institutes, laboratory networks, Africa CDC's regional structures and surveillance systems operating across the continent," she said. "The BRICS system will be most useful to us if these systems can communicate with each other and information can move quickly enough to support decisions on the ground." Raphael Obonyo, a Kenyan public policy analyst, said the proposed system could be particularly significant for Africa because it would help establish a common mechanism for tackling diseases and outbreaks, with a focus on prevention, detection and response. He said greater BRICS cooperation could strengthen disease surveillance, diagnostics, vaccine research and manufacturing, as well as technology transfer. "Most importantly, the cooperation will aid Africa in building resilience, innovation and sustainability in the prevention and response to mass infectious diseases," he said. Health is a key area of cooperation among BRICS members, with intensified joint efforts in collaboration in recent years in disease control and prevention, research and innovation and improving universal health coverage. Cooperation mechanisms such as the BRICS Tuberculosis Research Network and BRICS Vaccine Research and Development Centre have been established for member states to collaborate on research, technology transfer and capacity building. Beyond the early warning system, Africa CDC envisions opportunities for other practical cooperation projects between African and BRICS institutions. Several BRICS countries have strong capabilities in pharmaceuticals, vaccines, diagnostics, biotechnology and genomic surveillance. "We would like to see that translated into very practical cooperation with African institutions: joint research, stronger laboratory networks, clinical trials, training, technology transfer, partnerships between manufacturers and faster development of diagnostics and other medical countermeasures," Koly said. For Africa to benefit fully from the emerging cooperation with BRICS in disease prevention and control, Obonyo said institutions such as Africa CDC and national public-health agencies must ensure the necessary systems and capacities are in place to support timely detection and effective responses. African nations must also invest in preparedness before emergencies occur, including through stronger health systems, surveillance and cross-border coordination, he said.

item.title: Xi: China, India can achieve shared growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Xi: China, India can achieve shared growth Nations urged to provide positive energy for global peace, stability President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that China and India, although having different national conditions, can learn from each other's strengths to achieve shared success and pursue common development. He made the remarks when meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the capital of India. The two leaders had a candid and in-depth exchange of views, reaching an important consensus on China and India being partners. Xi said that amid a complex international situation, China and India — as the two most populous countries and important members of the Global South — bear significant responsibilities. Both countries should keep the future of humanity in mind and the well-being of their peoples at heart, and work together to promote the high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, providing more positive energy for world peace, stability and prosperity, he said. On the development of bilateral relations, Xi urged India to calibrate the direction with an objective and rational strategic understanding, saying that China and India are partners, not rivals, and they represent development opportunities for each other, not threats. Xi underlined the need for both sides to uphold a win-win approach to achieve mutual success. The two countries should expand cooperation in cultural and people-to-people exchanges, as well as increase direct flights, to improve the public opinion foundation of bilateral relations, he said, adding that the two nations should also adopt a balanced approach to address each other's economic and trade concerns. Xi urged eliminating interference with the political wisdom of mutual respect and mutual understanding, saying that the two countries should remain committed to a dual-track approach of advancing bilateral relations and resolving the boundary question, with both reinforcing each other and maintaining peace and tranquility in border areas. He also called for China and India to strengthen coordination within multilateral frameworks in addition to BRICS, such as the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and the Group of 20, and work together to address global challenges and staunchly defend international fairness and justice. During their meeting, Modi assured Xi that India always views its relationship with China from a strategic and long-term perspective. India is willing to be partners with China, rather than rivals, and is ready to view China's development as an opportunity, rather than a challenge, he said. Modi said that India adheres to an independent foreign policy, and its development of relations with China is not influenced by third parties. India's policy and stance on the Taiwan question and issues related to the Xizang autonomous region remain unchanged, and it will not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities in the country, he added. Modi expressed India's readiness to maintain high-level exchanges and strengthen strategic communication with China based on mutual respect and mutual trust, promote mutually beneficial cooperation, and encourage close cultural and people-to-people exchanges to achieve greater development in bilateral relations. He also expressed India's commitment to working with China to maintain peace and tranquility in border areas.

item.title: Xi attends BRICS summit in New Delhi
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
Xi says BRICS world's most influential platform for emerging markets cooperation NEW DELHI -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said here on Saturday that the BRICS cooperation mechanism has become the world's most influential platform for cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries. When addressing the Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Xi noted that this year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation, saying that over the past two decades, the BRICS cooperation mechanism has continued to grow and expand, and has demonstrated remarkable vitality and dynamism. Xi said it has been 20 years of self-reliance and self-strengthening, adding that BRICS countries have actively explored development paths suited to their own national conditions, setting an example of self-strengthening through unity among emerging markets and developing countries. This has also been 20 years of standing together through thick and thin, Xi noted. BRICS countries, Xi said, have worked together to tackle challenges ranging from the global financial crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic to climate change. The group has remained steadfast in safeguarding the common interests of the Global South, while providing the world with stability and positive momentum, he said. Xi also hailed the past 20 years of BRICS cooperation as fruitful, saying that BRICS countries have undergone a historic expansion, established a comprehensive, multi-tiered framework for cooperation, and ushered in a new stage of high-quality development for greater BRICS cooperation. Xi stressed that the world is undergoing accelerated transformation unseen in a century, the Global South is rapidly growing in strength, and the trend toward a multipolar world is unstoppable. Meanwhile, countercurrents of unilateralism and power politics are surging, multilateralism and the international order are coming under strain, and deficits in peace, development, security and governance continue to widen, he added. He said that BRICS countries should firmly stand on the right side of history, strive to be a pioneer of the times, steer the international order toward greater justice and equity, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity. Xi called on BRICS to pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development. BRICS countries, he said, should firmly seize the initiative, strengthen cooperation in artificial intelligence, encourage open-source development, openness, cooperation and sharing, and push practical cooperation into new areas and to new heights. BRICS countries are welcome to actively participate in the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, he said. China proposed an initiative to promote new industrialization through artificial intelligence among BRICS countries, and is willing to work with all parties to deliver more outcomes in research, development and application, and deepen cooperation in industrial and supply chains, he said. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in upholding peace and stability. BRICS countries should uphold a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, oppose the Cold War mentality and bloc confrontation, reject violations of other countries' sovereignty and interference in their internal affairs, and play a constructive role in resolving hotspot issues, making a distinctive BRICS contribution to finding solutions that address both symptoms and root causes, he said. Noting that the situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid, Xi said this war has inflicted serious losses on the people of all countries in the region, and it is against the common interests of the international community. Xi said he has set out four propositions on safeguarding and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East, which are aimed at de-escalation, ending hostilities and promoting peace. Xi urged relevant parties to keep to the direction of political settlement, and work for a permanent, comprehensive ceasefire. China will work with fellow BRICS members to play a due role in bringing peace and tranquility to the Middle East, he said. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in facilitating mutual learning between civilizations. The countries, he said, should champion the common values of humanity and advocate exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations as well as harmonious coexistence. They should ensure the success of the BRICS forum on people-to-people and cultural exchanges, share experience in state governance, and build positive momentum for the steady development of relations between countries, Xi added. Xi advocated efforts to deepen cooperation in culture, tourism and education, strengthen youth exchanges, and promote more frequent interactions and closer bonds among the peoples. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in reforming and improving global governance. He urged the group to keep pace with the trend toward greater democracy in international relations, promote a more just and equitable global governance system, and uphold the authority of the United Nations. Xi said BRICS should support a multilateral trading system centered on the World Trade Organization, and reject all forms of protectionist measures. The grouping should lead global governance in emerging domains such as cyberspace, outer space and the deep sea, and amplify the voice of Global South countries, he added. Over an extraordinary two-decade journey, solidarity and cooperation have remained the driving force behind the BRICS cause, Xi stressed. Xi called on BRICS members to remain sincere and candid with one another, seek common ground while respecting differences, and respect each other's core concerns. He also urged the group to deepen mutual understanding through communication and dialogue, properly handle differences, and ensure that BRICS cooperation continues to move forward steadily. China, Xi said, will take over as the rotating chair of the BRICS and host the 19th summit next year. The Chinese side stands ready to work with all parties to build consensus, create a better future, and embark on BRICS' third "golden decade," jointly opening up a bright future of prosperity and progress, he added. At the summit, all parties spoke highly of the development achievements made by BRICS over the past 20 years, noting that the BRICS mechanism has broad representation and great potential for development. In the face of escalating geopolitical conflicts and the rise of unilateralism, BRICS countries have a responsibility to speak up for the Global South, uphold multilateralism, support the central role of the United Nations, uphold the sovereign equality of all countries, abide by international law, oppose interference in the internal affairs of other countries, support free trade, and jointly address global challenges, they said. All parties should uphold the BRICS spirit, deepen cooperation across various fields, enhance economic resilience, promote a more just and inclusive international order, and build a secure and prosperous multipolar world, they added. All parties appreciated China's important contribution to the development and expansion of the BRICS mechanism and supported China, as next year's BRICS chair, in successfully hosting the 19th BRICS Summit, so as to jointly bring BRICS cooperation to a new level. The leaders also adopted a joint declaration at the summit.

item.title: BRICS: Building Bridges
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BRICS: Building Bridges Share - WeChat
President Xi Jinping has called for strengthening the foundation, momentum and impact of greater BRICS cooperation and delivering more practical benefits to the peoples. In recent years, China has advocated enhancing BRICS cooperation, delivering tangible results through concrete action. From doctors gaining new skills to businesses finding new markets and young people discovering new opportunities, BRICS cooperation is building bridges across borders, connecting people, markets and opportunities, and opening new pathways to shared development.
